newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Guangdong eyes 10 pct yr/yr rise in GDP.
newsitem.headline: China's Guangdong eyes 10 pct yr/yr rise in GDP.

text.p: China's booming southern Guangdong province, which borders capitalist Hong Kong, expects gross domestic product (GDP) to rise 10 percent year-on-year in 1997, official media said on Thursday.

The province's 1996 GDP was 609.7 billion yuan (US$73.46 billion), up 11 percent from 1995, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily quoted Guangdong Governor Lu Ruihua as telling a recent meeting of Chinese government officials.
Guangdong's retail price inflation was 4.4 percent in 1996, far below the target of 10 percent, he told the meeting.
Fixed-asset investment in Guangdong rose five percent year-on-year to 244.3 billion yuan in 1996, he said.
Foreign trade reached US$110 billion, including exports worth US$59 billion in 1996, Lu said. He did not give comparative figures.
An improvement in Guangdong's investment climate saw actual foreign investment in the province jump 15 percent to US$13.9 billion in 1996, Lu said.
"But Guangdong's economy faces problems such as the falling profitability of state-run enterprises, rising stockpiles, bad loans and blind investment," he said.
"The government will place agricultural development and economic structure reform at the top of its agenda this year," Lu said.
"Grain output will rise to about 19 million tonnes in 1997 on the government's drive to protect arable land," he said.
"Key sectors to be supported by the (provincial) government this year will include electronics, telecommunications, petrochemicals and machinery," Lu said but gave no further details. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
